<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The next task is implementing PATCH for tickets.

Jackson PATCH handling needs to distinguish omitted fields from null values. Null should mean unassign rather than omit. Status must be rejected. Empty bodies with no allowed fields must be rejected. Options include Optional, custom DTOs, Maps, Boolean flags, or JsonNode.

Optional<String> does not cleanly separate omitted fields from null. A mutable class with explicit presence flags and custom Jackson deserialization is the preferred approach. Adding a JsonNullable dependency is avoided unless necessary.

Java Optional cannot distinguish omitted fields from null values because Jackson deserializes both cases as Optional.empty(). This makes the Optional approach unusable for PATCH. The remaining options are a custom deserializer on a non-record class, manual JsonNode parsing, or a wrapper using @JsonMerge.

Using Optional fields inside a mutable class still leaves the Optional object itself as null when a field is omitted, so it cannot distinguish between absent and explicitly null values. The better approach is to use a dedicated request class with explicit presence flags, or to parse the raw JSON as a JsonNode and handle each field manually.

Plain record fields cannot distinguish omitted fields from null values. A class with Optional fields and custom Jackson configuration is being considered instead. Parsing the raw JSON as a JsonNode was rejected as unsuitable.

The chosen approach is a mutable class with boolean presence flags. Jackson invokes setters for every provided field, including null values, but skips omitted fields entirely. This cleanly distinguishes omitted from null for assignee. The controller will reject requests containing a status field, and return 400 for empty bodies lacking any allowed update field.

Field-level validation rules are being defined for PATCH updates. Title must be non-blank and no longer than 200 characters. Description must be non-blank and no longer than 10,000 characters. Assignee must be non-blank and no longer than 120 characters. Priority must be a valid enum value. Conditional Bean Validation is tricky for PATCH because @NotBlank rejects null, which would prevent omitting a field. The service layer will likely handle these checks directly.

Service-layer validation will replace Bean Validation for optional PATCH fields. @Size works on nullable fields, but @NotBlank cannot be used because it rejects null. Non-blank checks will run in the service when a field is actually provided. Unknown fields may be rejected, though the spec does not explicitly require this.

Jackson ignores unknown properties by default, so no extra rejection logic is needed there. The implementation will create `PatchTicketRequest.java`, update `TicketController` and `TicketService`, and mark T05 complete in the plan. The entity’s `@PreUpdate` timestamp will refresh automatically on dirty flushes, so no manual `updatedAt` bump is required.

Blank title or description values will trigger a 400 response. The `PatchTicketRequest` class is being drafted with explicit boolean presence flags for each field, paired with `@Size` constraints and `@JsonProperty` annotations.

The `PatchTicketRequest` class now includes `assigneePresent` and `statusPresent` flags alongside the other fields. Each setter marks its flag to detect whether the client provided that field. Getters expose the actual values and the presence flags. A `hasAnyUpdatableField()` helper returns true only when at least one allowed update field is present. A separate `isStatusPresent()` helper detects when the status field is included, which will be rejected.

A null priority value will be rejected as invalid, while a null assignee value will be treated as an unassignment. The service method will begin by throwing a 400 response when the status field is present in the request.

The service method now fetches the ticket by ID and throws a 404 if it is missing. It validates that at least one allowed update field is present, then begins processing the title field when it is provided.

The service method now applies concrete validation rules. Blank titles and descriptions trigger a 400 error. Titles longer than 200 characters are rejected. Valid titles are trimmed before assignment. Null priority values are rejected. Assignees are normalized through a helper method.

The service method will call `ticketRepository.save()` explicitly for clarity. Controller `@Valid` combined with `@Size` is sufficient for T05; T09 will tighten validation. Malformed UUIDs are handled by Spring as 400 errors. The plan will be updated to mark T05 complete. The build will be verified.
</details></think>

</summary>
```bash
set -e
# Create
CREATE=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/tickets \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Cannot reset password","description":"User gets 500 on reset link.","priority":"HIGH","assignee":"alex@example.com"}')
BODY=$(echo "$CREATE" | head -n -1)
CODE=$(echo "$CREATE" | tail -n 1)
echo "CREATE HTTP=$CODE"
ID=$(echo "$BODY" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['id'])")
echo "ID=$ID"
echo "$BODY" | python3 -m json.tool | head -20

# Patch one field
PATCH1=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X PATCH "http://localhost:8080/api/tickets/$ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Updated title"}')
echo "PATCH title HTTP=$(echo "$PATCH1" | tail -n 1)"
echo "$(echo "$PATCH1" | head -n -1)" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('title=',d['title'],'assignee=',d['assignee'],'priority=',d['priority'],'status=',d['status'])"

# Unassign
PATCH2=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X PATCH "http://localhost:8080/api/tickets/$ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"assignee":null}')
echo "PATCH unassign null HTTP=$(echo "$PATCH2" | tail -n 1)"
echo "$(echo "$PATCH2" | head -n -1)" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('assignee=',d['assignee'])"

# Unassign empty string
curl -s -X PATCH "http://localhost:8080/api/tickets/$ID" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"assignee":"bob"}' >/dev/null
PATCH3=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X PATCH "http://localhost:8080/api/tickets/$ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"assignee":""}')
echo "PATCH unassign empty HTTP=$(echo "$PATCH3" | tail -n 1)"
echo "$(echo "$PATCH3" | head -n -1)" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('assignee=',d['assignee'])"

# Reject status in body
PATCH4=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X PATCH "http://localhost:8080/api/tickets/$ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"status":"CLOSED"}')
echo "PATCH status reject HTTP=$(echo "$PATCH4" | tail -n 1) body=$(echo "$PATCH4" | head -n -1)"

# Empty body reject
PATCH5=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X PATCH "http://localhost:8080/api/tickets/$ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{}')
echo "PATCH empty reject HTTP=$(echo "$PATCH5" | tail -n 1) body=$(echo "$PATCH5" | head -n -1)"

# GET confirms
GET=$(curl -s "http://localhost:8080/api/tickets/$ID")
echo "$GET" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('GET title=',d['title'],'assignee=',d['assignee'],'status=',d['status'],'updatedAt=',d['updatedAt'])"

```
